bio.title: a smol death
bio.nowPlaying: Cute without the E by Taking Back Sunday
bio.body:
Sup 👋 my name is M.K. Muere & yes, my last name means death! 💀 I like to lead engineering teams and build cool shit on the internet. I've worked in both agency and product over the last 10 years, and have been a child of the internet for even longer!

Formality aside, I practice in digital witchcraft and internet buffoonery.

meta.title: CV / Resume | chibi.muere
meta.description: The CV and resume of M.K. Muere: a front-end tech lead and development manager based in Toronto. She specializes working in Shopify and headless stacks, with accessibility as top of mind.

heading.title: A record of the work.
heading.lede: I'm M.K. Muere, a front-end tech lead and development manager based in Toronto. Shopify stores and headless websites are what I build best. I also help web teams ship semantic code with accessibility top of mind, because the internet should be easy to navigate for everyone.
heading.printHint: Opens in a new tab: print it or save as PDF.

entries.description: Front-end tech lead for new and retaining Shopify clients. I help teams by ensuring only the best semantic, and accessible code makes it to production.

Joined as a senior dev in 2021 & stepped into development manager in 2022. Highlights: migrating Endy.com to headless Shopify (Next, Sanity, TS), automated scheduled deployments, and introducing agile workflow to the marketing dept.
Developed and managed Shopify storefronts of large enterprise clients.

The crux of my creative and technical opinions were formed here. The people and lessons I gained in this role have influenced my career tremendously. I think of my time here fondly. (Wordpress Gutenberg, Headless Shopify)

The company of creative geniuses that took a chance on a baby developer (me). At O/B I learned taste, creative ways to solve problems, how to cook a mean tortierre, and the importance of doing our best work for deserving clients. (WordPress, WooCommerce, a11y, bespoke designs)

Six years in IT service, vendor and license management, then a stint in the digital design team. During my time there, I reviewed over 130+ contracts in the span of a year for any discrepancies; resulting in $572K CAD of cost savings for 2014.

work.title: Things I'm proud of.
work.endy: Endy.com Site migration to headless Shopify with Next.js, Sanity CMS and TypeScript, automated scheduled deployments, and introducing an agile workflow to the Growth department.
work.munge: StudioMunge.com WordPress multisite, SVG animations, custom filtering, and a custom-built intranet inventory system. Won a Gold W3 Award for Architecture & Design, Silver W3 Award for Website Features, and nominated for a Webby Award.
work.clients: Also worked with ELTE, Mkt, Royal Conservatory of Music, Canadian Cancer Society, Canada Learning Code, Interac, Another Room, Happy Fairy Art, OPFA, Forest Ontario and Salad King.

practice.title: Ways of working.
practice.leading: Leading Development manager and tech lead on both agency and product teams: agile workflows, lunch & learns, and internal guides that help teams learn best practices.
practice.building: Building Shopify and headless JAMstack with Next.js, Sanity and TypeScript. At the end of the day, the tools don't matter, as long as the website is accessible, performant, and has smol moments of memorable delight.
practice.caring: Caring Semantic code with accessibility top of mind. I want to make the internet a better and easier-to-navigate space for everyone.

entries.description: Selected students of a women-only cohort hosted at Tulip. It was an accessible, judgement-free, and female-friendly space to learn software development.
Where I learned to turn a passion into a career. At HackerYou I learned frontend development fundamentals in the span of 3 months. I also took part-time courses for fullstack development.
In Japanese Language and Literature. This is my participation trophy to humble brag that I know enough Japanese, to confidently order off a sushi menu.
Bachelor of Technology. Girl, I went to school for print design and ended up in web development. Feel free to ask me how I got here, lol.
